# US News Map

> Search digitized American newspapers from the Library of Congress's Chronicling America collection and see where and when a word or phrase was printed. Each matching page is placed on the map where its newspaper was published and counted by date. The site and its JSON API are free and need no sign-in.

The newspaper pages come from Chronicling America (Library of Congress, with the National Endowment for the Humanities). The collection is still being indexed, so counts grow between index versions; [the dataset details page](https://usnewsmap.com/datasets) says how much is searchable now. Coverage is uneven: some states, years and languages have far more digitized pages than others, so compare a count with the number of pages published in the same place and dates before reading much into it. The text is OCR, so older pages have many misspellings and broken words.

## Site

- [Home and search](https://usnewsmap.com/): search results show on a map, with a timeline and a table. A search's address can be shared, for example `https://usnewsmap.com/?q=%22cross+of+gold%22&from=1896-06-01&to=1896-12-31`. The page needs JavaScript; to read results as data, use the API below.
- [Dataset details](https://usnewsmap.com/datasets): the collections in the index, where each comes from, its rights and how it is searched; how many of the downloaded pages are searchable, what the ingest pipeline is doing now, and page counts by state and by language. The same data is JSON at `/v1/status`.
- [Privacy](https://usnewsmap.com/privacy): what the site records. Search words are kept, but never with an IP address or anything else about who searched.

## API

Base URL `https://api.usnewsmap.com/v1`. The same routes answer at `https://usnewsmap.com/v1`. All routes are `GET` and return JSON. Errors are `application/problem+json` (RFC 9457) with a `type`, a `detail` and sometimes a `hint` on how to fix the request. On `/v1/aggregate`, `/v1/hits`, `/v1/places` and `/v1/coverage`, an unknown or repeated parameter is an error.

- `/v1/meta`: the dates covered (`bounds`), page, newspaper and place counts, the `index_version`, the query `limits`, and `languages`: each language code with its name and number of newspapers.
- `/v1/aggregate?q=...`: for one search, the total number of matching pages, a count per time bucket, counts per place, and per place per bucket. `series.baseline` gives the pages published in each bucket, matching or not, across the whole country or the `state` values given. It is `null` when `lccn`, `lang` or `front` is set, because the API has no exact page count to compare with then.
- `/v1/hits?q=...&place=<place id>`: matching pages from one place, oldest first, each with text snippets and a link to the page on loc.gov. `/v1/hits` needs either `place` or a single `lccn` (one newspaper). `limit` is 1 to 50 (default 50). When `next_cursor` is not null, pass it as `cursor` to get the next results. When `/v1/meta` has `"browse_pages": true`, `/v1/hits?lccn=<one lccn>` with no `q` lists every page of that newspaper by date (`sort=oldest` or `newest`; the other filters still apply), each with the opening of its text as its snippet. Its `next_cursor` goes on to the newspaper's last page, however many there are, where a search's last page is the one starting at result 10,000. Pass the cursor with the same `sort`. On a later page, `total` counts the pages from that one on. Otherwise `q` is required.
- `/v1/places`: every place as GeoJSON, with its name, state, how precisely it is located (`precision`: `city`, `county` or `state`), its number of newspapers and their languages. Place ids such as `P00001` are what `place` takes.
- `/v1/coverage?from=...&to=...&bucket=...`: pages published in each place per bucket, whether or not they match a search, for turning counts into rates by place. It also takes `state`.
- `/v1/status`: the ingest pipeline's progress.
- `/v1/titles`: every newspaper in the index, with its `lccn`, title, `place_id`, place, state, first and last year, page count and languages. `/v1/titles/<lccn>` returns one. Before searching, check here that the papers you need are in the collection. A town with no title has no local coverage, however you search.
- `/v1/days?q=...&place=<id>[,<id>...]`: matching pages per day for 1 to 20 places.
- `/v1/versions`: every index version that was built, and which one is being served.

Search parameters, shared by `/v1/aggregate` and `/v1/hits`:

- `q` (required, except for one newspaper's pages on `/v1/hits` as above): the search, up to 256 characters and 12 terms. Without `mode`, words are all required, a phrase goes in double quotes, `OR` joins alternatives (up to 4), a leading `-` excludes a word, and `word*` matches words that start with `word`, which needs at least 5 letters (`limits.min_prefix_chars` in `/v1/meta`). Inside a word, after the same number of letters, `?` matches exactly one character and `*` any run of characters, for OCR errors: `presi?ent`, `washi*ton`. A `?` at the end of a word is a question mark. Wildcards don't work inside quotes. `word~ocr` also matches the spellings OCR commonly gives a word (`president~ocr` finds `presldent` and `prefident`), and `2 OF (gold silver bryan)` matches pages with at least 2 of the words or phrases in the parentheses (up to 6 of them; `OF` in capitals).
- `mode`: `phrase`, `all`, `any` or `near`, for a plain list of words. `mode=near` also needs `near`, 1 to 20: how many words apart the terms may be.
- `from`, `to`: dates as `YYYY-MM-DD`. Dates outside `bounds` in `/v1/meta` are moved to the nearest bound.
- `state`: comma-separated two-letter postal codes, such as `GA,SC`.
- `lccn`: comma-separated newspaper ids (Library of Congress control numbers).
- `lang`: comma-separated three-letter language codes from the `languages` list in `/v1/meta`, such as `eng`, `ger` or `spa`.
- `front=true`: front pages only.
- `bucket`: `auto`, `year`, `month`, `week` or `day`.
- `fuzzy`: `1` or `2` matches single words within that many letter edits, for OCR errors. It does not apply to phrases (so not to `mode=phrase` or `mode=near`) or to `word*`; those stay exact. It only works when `capabilities.fuzzy` in `/v1/meta` is `true`; otherwise the API answers `422` (`/errors/unsupported`).
- `v`: an `index_version`. If it is not the one being served, the API redirects (307) to the current one.

## Response shapes

- `/v1/aggregate`: `total` has the counts (`hits` pages, `papers`, `places`, `days`) and the `first` and `last` matching pages, each with `doc_id`, `date`, `title`, `lccn`, `place_id` and `snippets`. `places` and `papers` hold parallel arrays: `places.id[i]` goes with `places.hits[i]`, and `papers.lccn[i]` with `papers.title[i]` and `papers.hits[i]`. `series` has `hits` and `baseline` per time bucket, and `bucket` says which buckets they are.
- `/v1/hits`: the pages are in `items`, each with `doc_id`, `date`, `title`, `lccn`, `place_id`, `edition`, `seq`, `front_page`, `snippets` (matches wrapped in `<mark>`, HTML-escaped) and `links.viewer`, the page on loc.gov. `total` counts every match for this place or newspaper, and `next_cursor` continues the list.
- A `doc_id` such as `sn83045462_1865-03-21_ed-1_seq-2` is the newspaper's `lccn`, the date, the edition and the page.

## Research recipe

To find every page about a subject:

1. Run one `/v1/aggregate` with the widest sensible dates and `bucket=year`. `total.hits` says how many pages match, and `total.first` is the earliest matching page.
2. For each id in `places.id` (or each `lccn` in `papers.lccn`), call `/v1/hits` with the same `q`, dates and filters, and follow `next_cursor` until it is `null`.
3. Keep the requests sequential and handle `429`, `202` and `503` as described below. Don't send them in parallel.

Searching for a person:

- Search the surname with one context word, such as a regiment, battle, town or office (`Kuder Waynesboro`, `Kuder "Livingston county"`), rather than the full name in quotes. OCR often misreads initials and ordinals: "Lieut. A. Kuder, 8th N. Y. cavalry" can come out as "Lieut. S. Kuder. Sth N. Y. cavalry", which `"Andrew Kuder"` or `"8th New York"` won't find.
- Try the titles and spellings papers used: `"Lieutenant Kuder"`, `"Lieut. Kuder"`, `"Capt. Kuder"`.
- `word~ocr` and `fuzzy` widen a search for OCR errors, but they are slower than a plain search. Use them on a narrow date range or with a filter.
- Read the snippets before counting a page. A common surname also matches other people with that name, and a search for a name and a town finds every page where both appear, even when they are unrelated.
- Check `/v1/titles` for the person's hometown papers. Chronicling America covers only some of each state's papers, so an obituary or a hometown report may not be in the collection.

## API usage guidelines

- Requests are rate limited per client address. A `429` comes with a `Retry-After` header; wait that many seconds before trying again. A `503` also has `Retry-After`; read its problem `type` and `hint`. `/errors/busy` means wait and send the same request again. `/errors/backend-timeout` means the search did not finish in time: narrow the dates or add filters before retrying, rather than repeating the same request.
- A search nobody has run recently can take a while. The API then answers `202` with `{"status":"computing"}` and a `Retry-After` of a few seconds, and keeps working on it. Send the same request again after that wait to get the result. Results are cached, so a repeated request is cheap.
- Prefer one `/v1/aggregate` request with a wide date range and a coarse `bucket` (such as `year`) over many narrow ones.
- Link people to the loc.gov pages that `/v1/hits` returns, so they can read the original newspaper.
